transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-22 16:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Ava Torres (Redwood CSM); Sarah Liao (Stratus Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Priya Narayan (Platform Eng), Elliot Zhang (PM)

Summary (auto): Outline POC timeline and success criteria for Stratus Insurance. Agree on benchmarks, access, and milestones including kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review, and exec readout.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, good to see you all. quick intros?
00:07 Sarah: yeah hi im sarah, head of ml at stratus, i've been working with priya and elliot on use cases, thanks for setting this up.
00:13 Carlos: carlos here, cto, i'll be high level but i'll check in on security and infra.
00:18 Maya: awesome. jonah from our side will lead the technical plan. jonah take it away for goals?
00:24 Jonah: cool thanks. so the ask we got was a short POC to validate inference economics and latency for your claims ingestion and anonymization pipeline, right? mostly batch+real-time mix?
00:35 Priya: yeah roughly. we have two workloads: a low-latency realtime endpoint for claim triage (~5 qps peak, p95 < 200ms for 512 tokens) and a batch scoring job (throughput oriented, 100k docs/day, avg 256 tokens).
00:50 Jonah: perfect that's helpful. on the realtime side we usually size for concurrency and KV cache behavior - sequence lengths matter - and for batch we look at throughput and quantized model configs.
00:59 Elliot: quick question, is KV cache the same as the key value cache? sometimes docs show K V cache as different thing.
01:05 Jonah: yes same thing, kv cache. some transcribers mess that up in notes.
01:09 Maya: ok so let's walk through success criteria - what would make this POC a win?
01:13 Sarah: for us a win is twofold: 1) meet latency targets for the realtime pipeline (p95 < 200ms end-to-end including network) and 2) show unit costs under our threshold (rough target: <$0.60 per 1k tokens for the workload mix) while preserving accuracy compared to our baseline model.
01:28 Carlos: and security: we need VPC/private deployment or dedicated with encryption, SOC2 artifacts, and audit logging; if that isn't met we can't move to prod.
01:38 Maya: totally, we can provide private endpoint options and our SOC2/ISO docs. we'll add those to the packet.
01:43 Jonah: on benchmarks we'll run two passes: latency microbench for p50/p95 tail on representative sequences, and a throughput/cost run with your sample dataset. we'll also do a quality check - generate outputs and compare against your baseline metrics (precision/recall or whatever you use).
01:58 Priya: for quality we're focused on entity replacement accuracy and hallucination rate. we'll send eval scripts.
02:03 Jonah: great. timeline wise propose a 4-week POC with these milestones: kickoff (week 0), access & baseline data handoff (days 1-3), initial bench & config (week 1), mid-point review with performance results (end of week 2), optimizations (week 3), exec readout + decision (end of week 4). does that align?
02:20 Sarah: sounds reasonable. what's required for access? VPC peering, SAML user accounts?
02:26 Maya: we support multiple options - private endpoint with TLS+mutual auth, VPC peering, or Dedicated deployment. for POC most customers use a private endpoint + customer-managed egress or short-lived creds. we can detail network diagrams in the security pack.
02:39 Carlos: we prefer VPC peering but will consider private endpoint if it's simpler to spin up. we need to know firewall ports and IP ranges.
02:46 Jonah: we'll include a checklist: IP ranges, ports, sample nginx proxy config, and IAM roles. also need a service account from you for the bench runs.
02:54 Elliot: timeline - you said mid-point review at end of week 2, what should we expect in that review?
02:59 Jonah: transparent metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), cost estimates extrapolated to your production load, and a quality regression report on the eval set. we'll also surface any operational issues (timeouts, memory pressure, batch sizing anomalies).
03:14 Maya: we'll book a 45-minute mid-point demo slot and invite your engineering and product leads.
03:19 Priya: for dataset handing over, we need a secure way to transfer. We can anonymize and drop PII - typically a S3 bucket with encryption, pre-signed links, or a secure share.
03:30 Jonah: pre-signed S3 works well. for private endpoints we can also do sftp over bastion if needed.
03:36 Sarah: ok we'll aim to deliver a week of sample logs by Friday.
03:41 Maya: perfect. on benchmarks, question about model variants - do we need to settle on a single model for the POC or test multiple?
03:48 Jonah: we recommend testing two variants: a cost-optimized quantized variant and a higher-accuracy float16 variant. that lets you see the latency/cost tradeoffs. we'll include recommended configs and quantization notes.
03:59 Carlos: curious about failure modes - if traffic spikes or a node is lost, what's the fallback?
04:05 Jonah: our runtime supports automatic routing to fallback model variants and burst capacity; for Dedicated we can pre-provision headroom. we'll document SLO behavior and graceful degradation.
04:16 Elliot: can you run a benchmark that simulates our peak 5 qps plus a batch window?
04:20 Jonah: yes we will script that mixture in the bench runner. prefer you provide sequence length distributions so we can synthesize realistic inputs.
04:28 Priya: noted. I'll export distributions by EOD Thursday.
04:32 Maya: pricing - we'll include a POC rate and a projected cost model for production at the end of the POC.
04:38 Sarah: do you offer credits or trial usage applied to Dedicated later?
04:41 Maya: we typically apply POC credits toward an initial committed capacity if you move to Dedicated within 60 days; details in the SOW.
04:48 Jonah: technical note: for p95 latency it's important to align on measuring locations. are you measuring from your app to the model or just model inference time?
04:55 Carlos: whole path. app -> inference -> response.
04:58 Jonah: ok we'll instrument client-side probes and model-side to isolate where time is spent.
05:04 Maya: let's recap milestones and dates:
05:07 Maya: 1) SOW & pricing sent by Oct 24.
05:10 Maya: 2) Kickoff and access setup week of Oct 29 (kickoff meeting Oct 29).
05:15 Jonah: 3) Initial bench & baseline measurement by Nov 5.
05:18 Jonah: 4) Mid-point review with results Nov 12.
05:22 Jonah: 5) Optimization and final runs Nov 19.
05:25 Maya: 6) Exec readout and decision week of Nov 24.
05:29 Sarah: those dates work for us tentatively, we'll confirm after the SOW.
05:33 Priya: a couple technical asks: do you provide per-token cost breakdowns and trace-level logs?
05:38 Jonah: yes per-token and per-route cost breakdowns, and we can enable tracing hooks for a subset of traffic. logs are auditable and available via the console or exported.
05:47 Carlos: compliance - can you share the SOC2 report and data residency statements?
05:51 Maya: we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs to the SOW email; we also include network diagrams and a short security FAQ.
05:58 Elliot: ok who is owner for each of those items?
06:01 Maya: action items as we listed - maya will send SOW, jonah bench plan, priya sample data. we'll capture this in the follow-up email.
06:10 Jonah: one more technical caveat: if you have long context windows (>2048 tokens) the runtime/kernel choices change, and we need to run a separate mem/latency profile.
06:20 Priya: our sequences are mostly <1024 but sometimes up to 1500. we'll flag those.
06:25 Jonah: noted, we'll include a 1500-token profile as part of the bench.
06:29 Sarah: ok that covers it. any blockers?
06:33 Carlos: none from me, just waiting on SOW and network checklist.
06:36 Maya: great, we'll send the SOW and security packet Thursday, propose kickoff Oct 29.
06:40 Sarah: thanks everyone.
06:42 Maya: thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invites.
06:45 (call ends)
